output: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Algeria on April 13, 2026, beginning an eleven-day visit to Africa. The visit aims to address themes of peace, migration, and interfaith dialogue. During his trip, Leo will visit Algeria, Cameroon, Angola, and Equatorial Guinea. This is his second major foreign trip as pope since his election in May 2022. The regions of Africa being visited are among the fastest growing in Catholicism in the world, with an estimated 288 million Catholics in Africa in 2024, making up over one-fifth of the world's total. His first stop in Algeria was marked by visits to ancient Christian sites and meeting with students from the Catholic University of Central Africa.

On April 15, 2026, President Donald Trump announced a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, following the collapse of talks with Iran. The United States Navy will enforce this blockade, which aims to prevent ships from entering or leaving the strait. Oil prices briefly rose above $100 per barrel before easing back to around $99 per barrel, and gas prices also increased. Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf joked about the situation, stating that Iran would "fight" if confronted militarily but would "deal with logic" if approached constructively. China expressed hope that the ceasefire would remain stable and emphasized its willingness to cooperate with all parties to ensure the uninterrupted flow of energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

On Thursday, March 12, 2026, the Tompkins Square Library in New York City hosted a concert by Musique Libre Femmes, featuring flutist Cheryl Pyle, saxophonist Ayumi Ishito, and pianist Roberta Piket. Attended by approximately fifteen people, the performance lasted about forty minutes and was introduced by the library's director of adult services, Jeffrey Katz, who highlighted the group's commitment to celebrating Women's History Month. Musique Libre Femmes, comprising experienced improvisers from the New York jazz scene, has recently performed at venues like the Lady Got Chops Festival, the Downtown Music Gallery, and various New York City jazz venues. The concert at Tompkins Square Library marked the group's first performance in the East Village.

On Tuesday, South Korean military officials announced they were suspending all drills involving small firearms after a stray bullet from a military exercise injured a young girl at a playground in Daegu. The incident, which occurred on Monday, saw the girl suffer a near-fatal injury but recover quickly and be discharged from the hospital. Investigations were launched into the incident, which took place during a shooting drill at a nearby military base. This comes a year after the South Korean Army mistakenly bombed a village near the North Korean border, causing civilian casualties. The latest incident has sparked discussions about the safety of civilians near military installations.

One Battle After Another, a film directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, won six Oscars at the 98th Academy Awards, including Best Picture. The film's director, Anderson, won Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay, while actor Sean Penn received his third Best Supporting Actor Oscar. Sinners, which earned sixteen Oscar nominations, won awards in four categories: Best Actor for Michael B. Jordan, Best Original Screenplay for Ryan Coogler, Best Original Score for Ludwig Goransson, and Best Cinematography for Autumn Durald Arkapaw. The film also marked the first time the Best Casting award was presented. Other winners included Jessie Buckley for Best Actress for Hamnet, Amy Madigan for Best Supporting Actress for Weapons, and Joachim Trier for Best International Feature for Sentimental Value. The ceremony was hosted by Conan O'Brien.

Caloundra won their round 3 game against Pine Hills 5-2 on Sunday at Meridan Plains, Queensland, Australia. Caloundra took an early lead with two goals in the first half, but Pine Hills equalized before halftime. In the second half, Caloundra scored four more goals to win the match. Jake Debbage and Mackenar Bradfield were the goal scorers for Caloundra, while Pine Hills assistant coach Daniel Cunha criticized his team's defensive lapses for the loss. Caloundra will host Mitchellton on Saturday, while Pine Hills will travel to Samford.

Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen allowed the use of dirtier fuel with elevated sulfur content for 60 days due to rising oil prices and supply issues caused by the Middle East conflict. This decision followed the prioritization of oil supply to farmers in rural areas and the release of 100 million liters from the reserve oil supply per month in response to a request from the International Energy Agency (IEA). The Australian government also announced the release of oil reserves to address the growing demand amid a supply shortage. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese commented on the situation, noting the need for long-term strategies to ensure fuel security, while President of the National Farmer Federation emphasized the criticality of diesel access for farmers to maintain agricultural activities and supply food to the nation. The country currently has reserves for 90 days of fuel under IEA obligations but fell short of this requirement. The opposition called for the government to bolster fuel security in light of these challenges.

On Thursday, March 12, 2026, United States President Donald Trump demanded the "unconditional surrender" of Iran on his Truth Social platform, following a week-long conflict with the country. Trump stated that once "acceptable" leadership was established in Iran, the US and its allies would bolster Iran's economy, making it stronger than ever. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian dismissed Trump's demand as a "dream" and vowed that Iran would retaliate against the US and its allies for the recent attacks. The conflict began when the US and Israel targeted Iran, killing key figures including the supreme leader, Ali Khamenei. Iran retaliated by attacking several Middle Eastern countries, including Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Oman. In response, the US military announced that the conflict could last four to six weeks.

The New South Wales (NSW) government announced plans to rezone a 113-hectare precinct in Burwood North, aiming to create a residential hub halfway between Sydney and Parramatta. The plan includes building 18,300 new homes and a new metro station to shorten commute times to just ten minutes. At least 5% of the homes are to be affordable housing for lower-income households. The new metro station, scheduled to open in 2032, will facilitate access to nearby retail outlets and businesses along Parramatta Road. The proposal also aims to create 3,900 new jobs during the implementation phase. The initiative is part of the Parramatta Road Corridor Urban Transformation Strategy and is being handled by the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that Australia will send an E-7A Wedgetail long-range reconnaissance plane and air-to-air missiles to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to aid in defending against potential attacks from Iran. The Wedgetail, capable of surveying 4 million square kilometers with its powerful radar, will be operated by around 85 Australian defense force personnel. In addition, Australia will supply the UAE with medium-range air-to-air missiles in response to their request, aiming to counter enemy drones. This move, while not initiating an attack, is interpreted by some legal experts as aligning with collective self-defense principles under the United Nations Charter, potentially making Australia a target for retaliation from Iran. The deployment comes in response to the UAE's call for assistance amid regional tensions.

Julio Teherán, a two-time MLB All-Star, announced his retirement from baseball at the age of 35 on Monday, March 11, 2026. He was scratched from a scheduled start for Team Colombia in the 2026 World Baseball Classic due to a shoulder injury. Teherán had a thirteen-year MLB career, during which he primarily played for the Atlanta Braves, but also played for the Los Angeles Angels, Detroit Tigers, Milwaukee Brewers, and New York Mets. Over his career, he compiled an 81-82 record, a 3.85 ERA, 1.223 WHIP, and 1,260 strikeouts in 1,470.2 innings. He had spent the 2022 and 2025 seasons playing in the Mexican Baseball League.

Moreton City Excelsior beat Caloundra 3-1 in a Football Queensland Premier League 2 match last Saturday. Brayden O'Regan scored twice for Moreton City, while Maxx Demerutis scored for Caloundra. Caloundra's Ethan Galbraith acknowledged that Moreton City is a tough team ahead of their next match.

On Tuesday, March 10, 2026, Australia granted refuge to five Iranian women's national soccer team players who refused to sing the Iranian national anthem during the Women's Asian Cup last week. If they had been deported, they faced potential punishment in Iran for their actions. Tony Burke, Australia's Minister for Home Affairs, stated that the players were welcome to stay in Australia for their safety. However, on Tuesday afternoon, the remaining Iranian players travelled to the Gold Coast airport by bus, and protesters surrounded the bus, lying on the ground to prevent it from moving. Local police worked with authorities to provide a safe place for the players and increased their presence while the players were traveling.

The Queensland Supreme Court ruled that the City of Moreton Bay Council acted unlawfully when it removed homeless campers from public parks last year. The court found that the council breached the law by not providing sufficient time for the homeless people to find alternative accommodation and by disposing of their personal belongings without consent. The Supreme Court ruled that the council's actions violated human rights. Although the eviction involved eight campers at Eddie Hyland Park, the legal case was brought by eleven applicants who said they were affected by the council's enforcement actions. The court noted that the council would still be allowed to remove campers from public parks, provided this was done lawfully. The council published a statement stating that eight homeless people had taken them to court and linking to the Supreme Court judgement. The council stated it would continue enforcing its ban on camping on public land and that responsibility for providing shelter to homeless people rested with the Queensland state government. Monta, a Danish firm, released its 2025 EV charger ranking on March 9, 2026, analyzing 260,000 connected chargers across Europe. The ranking was based on charger uptime and successful charge sessions, with AC and DC chargers ranked separately. The Mennekes EV charger topped the AC rankings with a score of 94.65, while five Alpitronic DC chargers scored the highest at 96.54. Monta noted that these rankings could motivate charger manufacturers to improve their products. Although Monta excluded chargers from Asia, Oceania, and North America from the ranking due to their smaller numbers, they plan to release quarterly updates and yearly reports with awards in 2026. Monta's EV charger ranking program began in June 2022.

On Tuesday, a rash on President Trump's neck, which had been visible in photos from a Medal of Honor ceremony the previous day, appeared to have been covered up with makeup. Dr. Sean Barbabella, Trump's physician, claimed the rash was concealed by a "very common cream." This is not the first time Trump has used makeup; he previously concealed bruises on his hands by claiming they were caused by excessive aspirin use.

Randwick City Council is seeking public input on whether to introduce parking fees at beaches within its jurisdiction, aiming to generate additional revenue for beach maintenance and improvement. The consultation, which began on March 6, 2026, will close on April 15. The council has already sent out paper copies to residents and set up an online form on its "Have Your Say" portal for those unable to receive the paper version. The proposal involves introducing parking fees at up to four beaches, aiming to cover estimated costs of A$3.6 million for installation and yearly revenue of A$6 million. Randwick includes several beaches such as Clovelly, Coogee, and Maroubra, with parking previously being mostly free but now subject to changes in some areas. The council expects to install new signage and parking meters by late 2026 and 2027 if the proposal is approved.

Caloundra FC won their first match in the Football Queensland Premier League 2 competition against Brisbane Knights FC 4-2 at home on Saturday, March 5, 2026. Ethan Galbraith, a Caloundra player, praised their quick start, attributing their success to their fast start and determination. The match was challenging for Brisbane Knights, who faced difficulties after being reduced to a player due to a foul in the first half. Caloundra coach Rob Shaw acknowledged the challenge ahead as they face Moreton City Excelsior next, while Brisbane Knights face Samford Rangers.

The Green Party's Hannah Spencer won a by-election in Gorton and Denton, Manchester, marking the first parliamentary win for the Green Party in the North of England and the first for the Green Party nationally since the 2019 European Parliament election. The election was a test for the Labour government, which has faced numerous scandals, and saw the Labour candidate receive only 25% of the vote, down from 50% in the 2024 general election. The Labour candidate's drop in support was the largest in the constituency's history, and the seat was previously considered one of the safest for Labour. The election also saw the Reform UK candidate, Matt Goodwin, increase his vote share by 15%, blaming the Green Party win on a coalition of Islamists and "woke progressives." The result has led to increased pressure on Labour leader Keir Starmer, with former Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner calling for his resignation amid mounting internal party pressure.

The news article discusses a musical performance presented by Striped Light in Long Island City, New York, featuring three experimental musical acts. On February 16, 2026, around forty to a hundred people attended the event, which took place in an undisclosed location. Jennifer Gersten performed as a soloist, playing the violin using various techniques. Jack Langdon played the Native American flute, exploring extended techniques and unusual sounds. John King and Leyya Mona Tawil performed as a duo, with King playing guitar and using electronics, while Tawil used electronics, microphones, and unconventional objects, leading to a high-volume set. The performance series, Striped Light, is curated by David Watson and Ian Douglas-Moore, with the location of the events kept secret from the public.

Caloundra FC have qualified for the next round of the 2026 Australia Cup preliminaries after defeating Pacific Pines 4-1 on Saturday night in Meridan Plains, Queensland. The victory came after Caloundra scored three goals in the span of ten minutes in the second half to secure their advancement. The team will now face Brisbane Knights in the opening round of the Football Queensland Premier League 2 on February 28. Caloundra captain Kaine Frew acknowledged that while the team is still gelling and learning to work together, they are confident in their ability to compete against stronger opponents like Brisbane Knights.

The Berlin exhibition "Gebaute Gemeinschaft - Göbeklitepe, Taş Tepeler and Life 12,000 Years Ago" opened on February 6, 2026, at the James-Simon-Galerie. It featured 93 archaeological artifacts from Göbeklitepe and Taş Tepeler, showcasing stone sculptures and everyday objects from 12,000 years ago. Curated by Barbara Helwing and Necmi Karul, the exhibition also included contemporary interpretations by Spanish photographer Isabel Muñoz. The exhibition, which runs until July 19, 2026, marks the first time some exhibits have been taken abroad after being displayed in several locations in Turkey.

The Tenkil Museum in Hanau, Germany, opened its latest traveling exhibition on February 7, 2026, titled "The Tenkil Catastrophe: Confronting and Healing." This event, the first of its kind to focus on the media's role in Turkey's "tenkil" (exclusion, expulsion, and eradication) abuses, attracted thousands of visitors. The exhibition features personal stories of purge victims, including Gülenists, through belongings like glasses and letters, as well as documents and testimonies from journalists. The Media & Tenkil section showcases media's involvement in documenting these human rights abuses. The Tenkil Museum has previously held exhibitions in Brussels, the European Parliament, Kassel, and Frankfurt.

The White House deleted a post on Donald Trump's social media account that portrayed former United States President Barack Obama and his wife Michelle Obama as apes. The video, which was shared by conservative meme creator Xerias, triggered backlash from American politicians, including from Trump's own Republican Party. After initially defending the post, the White House removed the video in response to backlash. The video, which lasts 62 seconds, portrays various Democratic politicians as animals, including former President Joe Biden, who is depicted as eating a banana. The video, which references allegations of electoral fraud in the 2020 United States presidential election, was shared on Xerias's account in October 2025.

On January 12, 2026, the Downtown Music Gallery in New York City hosted a public reading and discussion featuring Elliott Sharp and Joe Fonda. The event included an interview by Bruce Gallanter focused on their recently published books and was followed by a live performance by the duo. Sharp read from his new book, Feedback: Translations from the IrRational, and was then interviewed by Gallanter. Fonda discussed passages from his new book, My Life in the World of Music. The performance featured Sharp playing his electroacoustic guitar through an amplifier and Fonda playing his contrabass without amplification. The interview has been edited for clarity. Elliott Sharp picked up the guitar in 1968, initially playing psychedelic noise with influences from Cage's experimental music and electronics, inspired by artists like Jeff Beck and Jimi Hendrix. He started with blues rock but later moved towards more experimental and noise music, influenced by Cage's experimental techniques.

On January 13, 2026, an 11-year-old boy in Pennsylvania allegedly shot his father with a gun retrieved from a gun safe in the family home after becoming angry with him for telling him to go to bed. The boy was charged with criminal homicide and refused bail. He was placed in Perry County Prison and had an initial court hearing scheduled for January 22. According to court documents, the boy's mother was asleep when the gunshot woke her up and he told her, "I killed Daddy." The police arrived at the scene at 3:20 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (08:20 UTC) and found the boy shouting "Daddy's dead" and admitting he had shot his father. The boy told investigators he had taken a key from a drawer in the parents' bedroom to unlock the gun safe in an attempt to retrieve his Nintendo Switch, which had been placed in the safe. The Nintendo Switch had been taken from the boy by his father a few days prior

Bob Weir, the rhythm guitarist and vocalist for the iconic rock band Grateful Dead, passed away on January 15, 2026, at the age of 78. He succumbed to cancer, with his family announcing his death on Instagram, noting he had recently passed away due to "underlying lung issues." Weir was born in San Francisco, California, in 1947 and was a key figure in the band's music, contributing to hits like "Sugar Magnolia." He maintained a prolific solo career until his death, exploring various musical genres and collaborating with other artists. Weir's influence extended beyond the Grateful Dead, as he was a founding member of Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions, which evolved into the band that became known as the Grateful Dead.

Quinten Delaere, known online as 'kannotlogin,' uncovered cheating on the Roblox platform by demonstrating that top times were achieved using illegal scripts. He reported these findings on Reddit and collaborated with Roblox and Guinness World Records to verify the legitimacy of his own record-breaking attempt. Delaere's investigation revealed discrepancies in timestamps, missing digital items in the rival accounts' inventories, and discrepancies in theoretical maximum speeds, ultimately leading to the exposure of cheating. As a result, Guinness World Records officially recognized Delaere's achievement, marking the first time a Roblox player has received such recognition for exposing cheating. The recognition came after Delaere conducted a technical investigation, compiling a report that detailed his findings and arguments against the fraudulent records.

A Minneapolis woman died after being shot by an ICE officer in January 2026. The DHS stated that the woman attempted to run over officers with her vehicle, prompting the officers to fire in self-defense. However, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and Mayor Jacob Frey disputed this account, claiming the woman's actions were not aggressive enough to justify the use of deadly force. The incident is under investigation by both the BCA and the FBI. Minneapolis residents have protested against the presence of ICE officers in the city, and Mayor Frey has called for their immediate departure.

Manchester United fired Ruben Amorim as their head coach after just fourteen months in the role. The firing occurred after a tense conversation with Jason Wilcox, the team's director of football, regarding Amorim's preferred 3-4-3 style of play. The conversation quickly escalated, leading Amorim to express his desire to step down as manager and focus on his role as a coach. The dismissal came after a 1-1 draw against Leeds F.C. and followed comments made by Amorim at a press conference, where he stated he came to be "the manager, not the coach." Manchester United is currently sixth in the Premier League, trailing several teams closely in points, which led El Pais to describe their situation as "precarious." Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville expressed his disappointment, stating he expected better performance from the team.

A street in Kyiv will be named after the former Speaker of the Parliament Andriy Parubiy, who was killed in Lviv in August 2025 during the Russian invasion. The initiative to commemorate him was supported by 57% of participants in a public poll on "Kyiv Digital" application. The decision to name the street was made by the Kyiv City Council and on Facebook by Maryna Poroshenko, the leader of "European Solidarity," who announced the name on January 1, 2026. Parubiy was a prominent Ukrainian politician who served as the Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada from 2016 to 2019 and was posthumously awarded the Hero of Ukraine title in October 2025. He was killed in Lviv during the Russian invasion.

On January 4, 2026, the United States captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro at a house in Caracas, which was described as a fortress. The operation was justified by the US as a response to Maduro being the leader of the Cartel de los Soles and supporting illegal immigration into the US. The capture was part of a larger operation involving airstrikes targeting key locations, including La Carlota and Fort Tiuna, and resulted in civilian casualties. The CIA was reported to have infiltrated the Venezuelan government, and the operation was orchestrated by the US special forces, the Delta Force. Maduro was captured at 2:01 a.m. local time and relocated to a ship before being transported to the southern district of New York for prosecution. His wife, Cilia Flores, was also captured and both were on board the USS Iwo Jima (LHD-7) with destination the southern district of New York. Attorney General Pam Bondi stated

Tarique Rahman, the acting chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), returned to Bangladesh on December 25, 2025, after 17 years in self-imposed exile in London. His arrival marks a significant development in the country's political landscape following the ouster of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024. Rahman is the son of Khaleda Zia, the official chairperson of the party and former Prime Minister of Bangladesh. Upon landing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, Rahman was greeted by thousands of Bangladesh Nationalist Party supporters amid tight security. He addressed a rally, emphasizing national unity, inclusivity across religious lines, and the vision of a democratic and economically strong Bangladesh. He drew parallels to the country's 1971 war of independence. Rahman, aged 60, left Bangladesh in 2008 for medical treatment after being released on bail following 18 months in detention during the military-backed government's rule from 2006 to 2008

On Friday, a 38-year-old man attacked workers at a tire manufacturing plant in Japan with a knife and what authorities believe was bleach. Eight people were stabbed, and seven were injured when bleach was thrown at them. The attacker, who wore a gas mask, was arrested at the scene. The motive for the attack is unknown, but the attacker had some connection to the factory, possibly as an employee or former employee. The Yokohama Rubber Company factory in Mishima, which produces passenger car tires and employs about 1,000 workers, has not seen such a mass casualty attack before in Japan, where violent crime rates are generally low and weapon regulations are strict.

On Monday, December 26, 2025, a 65-year-old woman was fatally stabbed inside a Barnes & Noble bookstore in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, by a 40-year-old homeless man who claimed there was no cause for the attack and that it was due to a "fight or flight response." The suspect, who ran into the woods after the attack but was caught shortly afterward, stated he had no history of violent crime and was from Georgia, arriving by bus a week before the incident. He was refused bail and is scheduled to appear in court again in January.

On Monday, December 26, 2025, a Mexican Navy medical plane carrying a pediatric burn patient and seven others crashed into a bay near Galveston, Texas. At least six people died, including four Navy officers and two civilians, including the child. The aircraft, a twin turboprop Beech King Air 350i, lost contact with air traffic control for about ten minutes before crashing. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum expressed her condolences to the families of the deceased and the victims on board. The flight originated from Mérida, Yucatán, and was en route to Galveston to transport a child to Shriners Children’s Texas for specialized medical treatment. The crash occurred near the causeway connecting Galveston Island to the mainland, and Sky Decker, a yacht captain, helped guide police through the dense fog to rescue survivors. On December 25, 2025, hundreds of protesters clashed with police in New Delhi amid escalating tensions between India and Bangladesh following the lynching of a Hindu man in Bangladesh. Hindu nationalist groups, including the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP), led the protests and attempted to breach barricades near the Bangladeshi High Commission. The unrest was sparked by the killing of a Hindu man in Bangladesh last week, which led to widespread protests and diplomatic protests from Bangladesh. The Indian envoy to Bangladesh was summoned on December 25 in response to the violent protests and concerns over the safety of diplomatic missions. Tensions have also escalated following the death of Sharif Osman Hadi, a critic of India and former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who died in a Singapore hospital after being shot in Dhaka.

On December 15, 2025, a house in Salisbury, North Carolina, caught fire and exploded during a fire fight, injuring twelve firefighters and two civilians. All firefighters were released from the hospital by December 16, and seven have returned to full duty. The explosion, caused by a gas line, compromised the house's structure, resulting in its roof collapsing. The Salisbury Fire Investigation Taskforce is investigating both the initial fire and the subsequent explosion, which displaced multiple residents and required assistance from the American Red Cross. Mayor Tamara Sheffield expressed her gratitude to the firefighters and expressed the city's sympathy to the family who lost their home.

The National Bureau of Investigation of the Philippines (NBI) has requested an Interpol Red Notice against former Ako Bicol Representative Zaldy Co, seeking his provisional arrest for extradition or similar legal action. The request stems from two graft cases and a malversation case filed against Co and other officials in relation to a flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro, as reported by the Manila Bulletin. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. revoked Co's passport on December 10, removing his legal basis to stay abroad. The Department of Justice has not confirmed whether a Red Notice has been issued for Co. Co left the country around the time the 20th Congress began its session in July. Recently, he released short videos accusing President Marcos and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez of inserting 100 billion Philippine pesos worth of projects into the 2025 budget.

Blaise Metreweli, the new head of the United Kingdom's Secret Intelligence Service (MI6), warned in her first public address in London on Monday that the UK is operating in a "grey zone" warfare space amid rising tensions with Russia. She accused Moscow of employing aggressive tactics such as state-sponsored arson and sabotage, as well as using drones to buzz airports and bases. Metreweli also addressed the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, stating that Russian President Vladimir Putin is dragging out negotiations and seeking to subjugate Ukraine rather than engage in genuine peace efforts. She emphasized the need for MI6 officers to blend traditional tradecraft with new technologies, particularly AI, stating technological mastery will infuse everything they do. Metreweli also noted that NATO countries have been supplying Ukraine with military and intelligence assistance since Russia's invasion in 2022.

Iceland has decided not to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest 2026 due to domestic public debate and reactions to Israel's participation. The decision comes after Iceland's broadcaster, RÚV, sought a vote on Israel's participation at the EBU's general meeting, which was declined. The EBU had previously approved changes to voting rules in response to allegations of vote manipulation by Israel, but did not take action to exclude any broadcaster.

Preston North End drew 1-1 with Coventry City at Deepdale on Tuesday, December 11, 2025. Coventry City won the match in the 70th minute when Jack Rudoni scored an own goal after his shot hit North End player Andrew Hughes. In the 77th minute, Daniel Jebbison of North End scored the equalizer with a goal assisted by Pol Valentín. Coventry City's Liam Lindsay was sent off in the 77th minute for a foul on Haji Wright. According to BBC Sport's user-submitted player ratings, Preston North End goalkeeper Daniel Iversen was rated the player of the match, while Matt Grimes of Coventry City was the top-rated player. The match was part of the 2025-2026 Sky Bet Championship season. Coventry City manager Frank Lampard expressed his frustration at not winning the match.

Four countries, including Spain, the Netherlands, Ireland, and Slovenia, withdrew from the Eurovision Song Contest 2026 due to concerns over neutrality due to the ongoing conflict in Gaza and the humanitarian crisis there. The decision was made in response to the European Broadcasting Union confirming Israel's participation, citing a loss of neutrality and the impact of the war. The broadcasters cited the need to prioritize the "humanitarian crisis" in Gaza and expressed concerns over the geopolitical influence on the contest. The withdrawals generated significant turmoil within the contest, with Spain being a part of the "Big Five" financial generators of the competition. The decision also led to new rules limiting government influence and imposing limits on public votes. Despite the boycott, Austria, host of the contest, and several other countries supported Israel's participation, viewing it as a cultural event rather than a political one.

On Friday, November 21, 2025, flutist Robert Dick and double bassist Mark Dresser reunited at the Fridman Gallery in New York City for a performance that was part of an art exhibition titled "House of Spirits," running from October 29 to December 6. The performance, lasting approximately 52 minutes, showcased Dick's versatility on the bass flute, piccolo, and a modified flute with a Glissando Headjoint, which he used to explore extended techniques such as multiphonics, glissandi, key percussion, and air sounds. Dresser, meanwhile, employed various techniques on the double bass, including two-handed tapping and percussive sounds, creating a rich tapestry of sound. The performance took place amidst the art exhibition, with the gallery's seating filled to capacity. Following the performance, Dick reflected on their past collaborations and their ongoing musical evolution, hinting at their deep history and the influence of their individual journeys

On November 29, 2025, a liquor store employee in Ashland, Virginia found a raccoon passed out in the store after a drunken rampage. The raccoon had broken into the store through a ceiling tile while it was closed and fallen onto a shelf where scotch and whiskey were stored. This was not the first time such an incident occurred; in 2013, a feral pig stole three six-packs of beer in a camping area near the De Grey River in Australia. The raccoon, now sober after a few hours of sleep and zero signs of injury, was released back into the wild. Raccoons have adapted so well to urban areas that a recent study found they have developed traits resembling those of domesticated animals, such as shorter snouts, smaller teeth, floppier ears, curlier tails, and reduced brain size. These traits are attributed to their ability to survive on human refuse.

Barnaby Joyce, a long-time Australian politician and Member of Parliament for New England, announced his resignation from the National Party on Wednesday, December 3, 2025. This decision came after a month of speculation and discussions with Pauline Hanson's One Nation party about a potential defection. Joyce, who had been a member of the National Party for 30 years, will continue to sit as a crossbencher until the end of his term in 2028 despite his decision to leave the party. He cited being relegated to the "ejection seat" as his reason for leaving, referring to the closest seat to the crossbench where independents sit. Joyce also expressed his consideration of defecting to One Nation and considered retiring from politics to pursue a career in the private sector. He criticized the National Party leadership for failing to communicate effectively with him, particularly during his decision-making process. Joyce expressed his regret for the "hurt" his resignation would cause and apologized for it. However

The World Service Authority (WSA) has achieved recognition from several sovereign states through a combination of historical documents and, in some cases, ongoing diplomatic efforts. They claim to have case-by-case endorsements from 185 countries, although verification for many of these claims is not publicly available, and some of the recognitions are from governments that no longer exist. The most notable recognitions include letters from countries like Upper Volta (now Burkina Faso) in 1972, Mauritania in 1975, Zambia in 1973, and Tanzania in 1995. The recognition from Tanzania was independently verified by Wikinews through the Embassy in Japan.

The WSA's founder, Garry Davis, passed away in 2015, and his protégé, David Gallup, became the President of WSA. Gallup discussed the organization's efforts to obtain recognition and shared his vision for the future. He elaborated on WSA's support for refugees, addressing criticisms that some have expressed about its

On November 20, 2025, a shooting occurred at a Benihana restaurant in Maple Grove, Minnesota. One person was injured, and the suspect fled the scene before police arrived. The victim, a 33-year-old man, was treated at a local hospital for non-life-threatening injuries. Authorities have not yet identified a motive for the shooting, but both the victim and suspect were known to each other. The suspect fled the area in a vehicle after the incident. No arrests have been made as of November 18, 2025.

Wikinews attended a Veterans Day event in New Chapel Hill, Texas, on November 20, 2025. During the ceremony, 21 military veterans and one Army National Guard member were honored, with each branch receiving applause as its name was announced. Roughly 480 people attended the event, which honored veterans and current military members. The holiday, observed on November 11, began as Armistice Day and recognizes all branches and eras of the US Armed Forces. In Texas, communities held ceremonies, parades, and moments of silence to honor veterans and reflect on their sacrifices. The school's band played the theme for each branch while students displayed the flags. Students displayed the flags of the U.S. Air Force, Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard, with veterans from all except the Coast Guard present on stage. On Wednesday, November 20, 2025, New York Police Department commissioner Jessica Tisch agreed to stay on as commissioner under mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani. Mamdani had faced criticism during his campaign for past comments advocating for defunding the police. The outgoing mayor, Eric Adams, praised Mamdani's decision, stating that by keeping Tisch, he recognized the effectiveness of their public safety efforts. However, a police reform group criticized Mamdani's choice, viewing it as a betrayal of his promises to New Yorkers.

On November 11, 2025, a Turkish military transport plane crashed near the Georgia–Azerbaijan border, killing all 20 military personnel onboard. The aircraft, a C-130 Hercules, vanished from radar 27 minutes after takeoff from Azerbaijan and crashed into Georgian airspace. The cause of the crash remains under investigation, with Turkish and Georgian authorities cooperating in the inquiry. Eyewitnesses described the aircraft breaking apart mid-air before spiraling down. The wreckage was found near the border region on November 12, and the flight recorder was recovered on November 13. Following the crash, Turkey grounded its fleet of C-130 planes as a precautionary measure.

The 2025 Queens World Film Festival took place from November 6 to 9 in Queens, New York City, at the Museum of the Moving Image. A breakfast and awards ceremony honoring Warrington Hudlin were held on November 8. During the event, filmmakers discussed ideas with financial professionals, and an audience reacted positively to a screening of The Caravan, a film about the struggle for affordable insulin. The festival opened on October 15 with the presentation of the 2025 Spirit of Queens award to Warrington Hudlin. Festival organizer Katha Cato emphasized the importance of freedom of speech and the need to continue telling stories that represent diverse voices, especially in the face of fear and censorship.

Bruce Chadwick, a professional magician and illusion builder from Fort Worth, Texas, shared his journey into the world of magic, including his first encounter with magic at age 8, being influenced by Charlie Dodson and the Story Brothers, and performing during his college years. He discussed his education at Baylor University, where he majored in Religion and Theatre Arts, and his career as a magic dealer and performer. Bruce also revealed his expertise in creating illusions, explaining that he learned the craft by designing and constructing magical effects himself.

The organizers coordinated with artists through a combination of direct communication and digital platforms to ensure that the exhibitions were set up and promoted effectively despite the restrictions. They also organized workshops and discussions to engage the audience more deeply with the artworks and the themes behind them.

Viktor Pinchuk, the photographer featured in the article, shared his experiences from participating in the "Night of the Arts" event in Simferopol, Crimea. This year, he held two exhibitions: one at the Central Museum of Taurida and another at the Museum of the History of Simferopol. Despite the challenging circumstances due to the complex and somewhat militarized situation in the country, the event still managed to attract a receptive audience interested in his photography, which explores his passion for traveling, documenting, and exploring the world.

Pinchuk noted that while there were differences compared to previous years due to restrictions, the event maintained its spirit of cultural and educational celebration. The organizers coordinated with artists

Zohran Mamdani, a Democratic Socialist, won the mayoral election in New York City on November 7, 2025, defeating former governor Andrew Cuomo. Mamdani led the polls for weeks and secured victory in the Hamilton Heights part of Manhattan. Voters expressed their support for Mamdani, citing his ability to listen to constituents, his diverse voter base, and his commitment to change. Maria Nuñez, a new citizen, voted for the first time and credited Mamdani's campaign for motivating her to vote. Others cited affordable housing and educational accessibility as key issues motivating their support for Mamdani. City Council candidate Edafe Okporo criticized the lack of community connection among those working on a nearby housing project, highlighting the disconnect between politicians and their constituents.

India defeated South Africa by 52 runs in the 2025 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup final, held at Navi Mumbai's DY Patil Stadium on November 4, 2025. India's Shafali Verma was named Player of the Match and Deepti Sharma received the Player of the Series award for their all-round performance. South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt praised India's brilliant cricket, acknowledging they outplayed her team.

The 35th annual Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade took place on October 19, 2025, with participants required to sign up in advance and check in at the event. At 3 p.m. New York time (19:00 UTC), a car drove through the crowd on 10th Street, honking and attempting to navigate through a dense crowd of pedestrians, dogs, strollers, and children. The driver, who had taxi and limousine plates, faced no intervention from police despite angry onlookers confronting the vehicle. The streets were crowded with dogs and people on several streets, including 6th and 10th Streets, and there were stalls for dog activities in the park. Izzy, a dog purportedly running for president, also attended the event.

On October 11, 2025, Kembra Pfahler of The Voluptuous Horror of Karen Black performed at MoMA PS1 as part of Vaginal Davis' exhibit, "Magnificent Product." The performance took place in the museum's courtyard and was preceded by an email to Eventbrite ticket holders advising attendees to arrive early to avoid missing part of the show due to expected high attendance. Despite a brief rain shower, the weather cleared, and the courtyard filled with audience members who were allowed to stay until the museum closed after the performance. The set included a mix of old and new songs, with Pfahler and Alice Moy throwing underwear into the audience during the song "Underwear Drawer." The performance ended with Pfahler inviting the audience to come on stage for mingling and photos until the museum closed. Police in South Australia have launched a taskforce to search for missing four-year-old August "Gus" Lamont, who disappeared on September 27. The taskforce, named Taskforce Horizon, includes specialists who will resume investigations into the situation. Gus is described as a white boy with curly blonde hair, wearing a blue Minions shirt, grey hat, light grey pants, and boots. He was last seen playing in his backyard before disappearing. Searches conducted the night of his disappearance found no results, and additional searches covering a two-and-a-half kilometre radius also failed to locate him. Yorke Mid North Superintendent Mark Syrus described Gus as "quiet" but "adventurous," and stated that he walked further from the property before getting lost. The family searched the area before contacting authorities, and Commissioner Stevens confirmed there was no indication of foul play. Hak Ja Han, leader of the Unification Church in South Korea, was arrested on September 26, 2025, on suspicion of bribing the first lady of South Korea and a conservative lawmaker. The 82-year-old leader was questioned the previous Wednesday, September 17, regarding allegations that she and her organization bribed Kim Keon Hee and Kweon Seong-dong with Chanel handbags and a diamond necklace valued at 80 million won (approximately $57,900). Prosecutors allege that Han and her church worked with a former official to send a 100 million won payment to Kweon. Han denied the accusations, claiming the former official acted independently. On Monday, she appeared before the Seoul Central District Court for an hours-long hearing, during which she declined to answer questions from reporters. Brett James, an American country music singer, songwriter, and record producer, died in a plane crash in North Carolina on September 18, 2025. The crash occurred in Franklin, North Carolina, near the Blue Ridge Mountains, and involved a Cirrus SR22T aircraft. Two other people also died in the crash. The National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation into the cause of the crash, with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) also involved. James co-wrote Carrie Underwood's song Jesus Take the Wheel, which won a Grammy Award for Best Country Song and was nominated for Song of the Year.

On Tuesday, a New York judge dismissed two terrorism-related charges against Luigi Mangione, who is accused of killing Brian Thompson, the CEO of United Healthcare. The judge ruled that prosecutors had not provided sufficient evidence to support these charges. Mangione will now face a murder charge, which the judge determined was not terrorism-related since Mangione did not make any demands or seek any particular governmental policy change. The Manhattan district attorney's office plans to proceed on the remaining nine counts, including murder in the second degree. Mangione is currently in custody and faces federal murder charges, which could carry the death penalty.

Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been sentenced to 27 years in prison for leading an armed criminal organization, attempting to overthrow the government, and other charges related to an alleged plot to disrupt the 2022 election. The sentence was handed down by the Supreme Federal Court on September 15, 2025, after four out of five justices voted to convict him on all counts. The charges stem from an alleged plot to assassinate President-elect Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes. Bolsonaro's co-conspirators were also convicted. The dissenting justice, Luiz Fux, argued there was no evidence that Bolsonaro was aware of or involved in the plot.

On Tuesday, October 1, 2024, federal authorities charged a man named Ryan Wesley Routh, 58, with attempting to assassinate former U.S. President Donald Trump on September 15 at Trump International Golf Club in West Palm Beach, Florida. Routh faces multiple charges, including attempting to assassinate a presidential candidate, possessing a firearm to carry out a violent crime, assaulting a federal officer, and criminal possession of a firearm. If convicted, he could face life in prison. Investigations suggest Routh planned the attack with intent and had written a note detailing his plans. Routh had previously been arrested and convicted in 2002 for possession of a machine gun, though he was not incarcerated for this offense. U.S. Attorney General Merrick Garland condemned the act, stating that violence targeting public officials endangers the democratic principles of the United States.

On Tuesday, September 24, 2024, a series of explosions occurred in southern Beirut and the Bekaa Valley, Lebanon, targeting Hezbollah, a Shia Islamist political party and paramilitary group. The explosions, which included pager and walkie-talkie detonations, resulted in twelve deaths and over 2,800 injuries. Early evidence suggested the blasts were triggered by explosives planted in the devices or faulty batteries. The following day, additional explosions occurred, killing twenty people and injuring 450, and damaging radios, laptops, and other communication devices. Consulting firms Predicta Lab and Le Beck suggested hardware tampering was likely involved, ruling out a cyber attack as the cause. Early investigations indicated the pagers contained pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN) and metal balls, possibly added for increased explosive effect. Drew Wolfendale, the Fusion Party President, was interviewed by Wikinews regarding the party's foundation, core values, and his personal journey into politics. The Fusion Party, formed by the merger of several former federal parties in 2021, is known for its emphasis on six core values: personal liberty, progress, ecological harmony, transparency, accountability, and innovation. Wolfendale, who has a background in engineering, finance, and economics, joined the party in 2017 due to its commitment to evidence-based policy-making. His contributions to the party include his engineering expertise, which he applied to problem-solving within complex systems, particularly in the railway industry, and his role as a Director at Humanists Australia. Despite not being elected to the Senate, Wolfendale remains dedicated to the Fusion Party's mission to promote a more effective form of representative government.

American rapper Lil Nas X has pleaded not guilty to four new felony charges of assaulting a police officer in Los Angeles on August 25, 2025. The charges stem from an incident on August 21, 2025, where Lil Nas X allegedly struck an officer twice in the face and resisted arrest. He was hospitalized briefly for a possible overdose before being booked at a county jail. His bail was set at $75,000. Lil Nas X has previously disclosed in social media posts that the past few years had been particularly difficult for him, but he is now aiming to regain confidence in his music and creativity.

German unemployment has reached 3 million for the first time since 2015, according to preliminary data released by the Bundesagentur für Arbeit (BA) on Friday. The national unemployment rate increased to 6.4% in August, up from 6.3% in July, marking the first time the mark has been reached since February 2015. The number of unemployed reached 3,025,000, while the broader underemployment figure stood at 3.634 million, an increase of 25,000 from the previous month. The inflation rate rose to 2.1% in August, exceeding analysts' estimates of 2.0%. The labour demand in the primary market declined, with 631,000 job openings reported in August, 68,000 fewer than the same month last year. The Federal Employment Agency Job Index (BA-X) remained unchanged at 98 points. On August 30, 2025, Sergey Markov, a former Russian parliament member and political analyst, was designated as a "foreign agent" by Russia's Justice Ministry. This move came after he served as a translator for the Russian government's stance on the invasion of Ukraine, as cited in major Western media outlets like The New York Times and Bloomberg. Markov criticized the designation, calling it a political move against him and those who oppose Putin's policies. He also pointed out a connection between his designation and his participation in a media forum in Azerbaijan, where he praised President Ilham Aliev. Previously, Markov had faced criticism for supporting Azerbaijan amid strained relations with Russia. His designation as a "foreign agent" stems from his support for measures against entities labeled as "foreign agents" in Russia, highlighting the irony of his situation.

Ronnie Rondell Jr., a stunt performer known for appearing on the cover of Pink Floyd's 1975 album Wish You Were Here, died at 88 in August 2025. He was set ablaze for the photo shoot on the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank, California. Despite wearing fire retardant clothing, his mustache was destroyed, and his face was burned. Rondell sustained numerous injuries throughout his career, including concussions and broken ribs, and once said, "You never told anyone you were hurt because they always had another guy that could fit the clothes." He retired in 2000 but continued working in films like Lethal Weapon, Thelma and Louise, Batman & Robin, Twister, and Star Trek: First Contact. Rondell left behind a wife and a son.

On August 8, the High Court in Kampala, Uganda, denied bail to opposition politician Kizza Besigye and his ally Obeid Lutale, who are facing a treason case. The court determined they did not meet the six-month remand period required for bail, based on their detention dates. Legal experts expressed concern over the ruling, with Senior Counsel Peter Walubiri criticizing the decision as favoring the state. Nicholas Opiyo suggested the ruling reflected political pressure, referencing past criticism by President Yoweri Museveni. Besigye's lawyer, Lukwago, condemned the ruling as disastrous. The pair's legal team argued their detention started in November 2024, reaching the six-month requirement by May 28, 2025, but the prosecutors countered that the case began in February 2021 when they were formally charged with treason at the Chief Magistrate's Court in Nakawa.

On Friday, August 6, 2025, a tractor trailer carrying thousands of hotdogs collided with two other vehicles on Interstate 83 in York County, Pennsylvania. The crash caused the hotdogs to spill onto the road, resulting in several injuries. Cleanup efforts involved raking up the hotdogs, which were slippery and caused traffic delays. The incident resulted in over one thousand pounds of hotdogs being lost. The Pennsylvania State Police are investigating the crash.

Summer Streets returned on August 3, 2025, with miles of roadway blocked off from car traffic for the annual program across Manhattan. Starting July 26 and running each Saturday through August, the car-free stretch included the Brooklyn Bridge up to Inwood for the first time. The event featured live music, arts and crafts tables, water bottle refilling stations, and softball batting cages. New Yorkers enjoyed cycling, running, rollerblading, and scootering along the route, which was partly sunny with temperatures around 74°F (23°C). The event took place on August 9 and 16, and two small routes in Brooklyn and the Bronx on August 23.

On July 30, 2025, Nigerian officials reported that abductors killed 33 to 35 hostages in Banga village, despite having paid a ransom. The hostages were reportedly slaughtered like rams, and the local government chairman described the killings as senseless and heartless. The hostages were abducted in February and 18 were released, while the remaining 51 to 56 were killed. The government made it a criminal offense to pay ransoms in 2022, intending to disrupt a lucrative kidnapping industry, but no arrests have been made in connection with these charges as of 2025.

Three people were killed and several more injured when a train derailed and crashed in a sylvan area in southwest Germany on Sunday evening. The crash occurred near Riedlingen in Baden-Württemberg, close to Ulm and Biberach. Authorities are investigating the cause of the derailment, which may have been triggered by a landslide caused by heavy storms. Two carriages derailed after striking debris, climbed an embankment, and crashed into trees. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed his condolences and offered support to the rescue services.

On Friday, July 24, 2025, Democratic Minnesota state senator Nicole Mitchell was convicted on two charges, felony first-degree burglary and possession of burglary or theft tools, stemming from a 2024 incident in which she was arrested after allegedly breaking into the home of her "estranged" stepmother in Detroit Lakes. Her lawyer argued that she entered the property to check on her stepmother's well-being, not to commit theft. Prosecutors presented body camera footage of Mitchell telling officers, "I know I did something bad," and argued her recorded statements contradicted her trial defense. The jury convicted her on both counts, and she faces a minimum of 180 days in jail. Governor Tim Walz's office anticipates Mitchell's resignation.

The UK government plans to lower the voting age to 16, following successful reforms by Scotland and Wales. The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government announced plans to allow 16- and 17-year-olds to vote in upcoming elections. According to official data, there are approximately 1.6 million 16-17-year-olds in the UK eligible to vote, compared to 48 million eligible voters aged 18 and above. Prime Minister Keir Starmer supports the changes, citing that 16-year-olds are old enough to work and pay taxes. The move aligns with the Labour Party's manifesto promise from the 2024 general election. A poll found that 51% of 16-17-year-olds support the change, with 33% likely to vote Labour. Critics include Nigel Farage, who argues that 16-year-olds should not be able to vote unless they can stand as candidates. On July 11, 2025, a man was hospitalized in critical condition after his vehicle went airborne twice in a roundabout crash in Fort Wayne, Indiana. The incident occurred at 7:30 a.m. local time (1130 UTC) at the roundabout located at Adams Center Road and Wayne Trace. The man was driving at high speeds, swerving, and passing other vehicles before striking a curb, causing his vehicle to become airborne twice. The vehicle first went airborne after hitting the curb, then hit a barricade marked 'road closed' before coming to rest in a field. The man was in a life-threatening condition at Lutheran Hospital. The Allen County Sheriff’s Department is investigating the incident.

On July 9, 2025, Russia launched a record-breaking drone and missile attack on Kyiv, killing one person and injuring 26 others. The attacks lasted until around 4:30 a.m. local time on Friday. The Ukrainian air force reported that 539 drones and missiles were launched during the assault, the highest number launched in a single attack since the start of the invasion. The strikes came hours after a call between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, during which Trump expressed disappointment that Putin was not ready to end the war. The Kremlin stated that it would continue the war in Ukraine until it addressed what it called "the root causes of the war in Ukraine."

A 20-year-old astrophotographer from Washington State captured a rare solar eclipse on Saturn using a telescope. Adam Smadi planned the image days ahead and took it on June 1, using Stellarium software to pinpoint when Saturn's largest moon, Titan, would cast a shadow across the planet's surface. He set up his 9.25-inch telescope at about 1 a.m. PDT (08:00 UTC) so the optics could cool to the outdoor temperature. By 3:30 a.m. PDT (10:30 UTC), Saturn was high enough to begin taking photos. He used a ZWO ASI662MC astrophotography camera with an infrared filter. The resulting image shows Titan's small dark shadow crossing Saturn's pale surface, with three other moons, Dione, Tethys, and Enceladus, appearing as tiny dots near the rings.
